acceptance: update_item with not_before set to an empty string clears the hold and the item is claimable immediately (test or live proof)
A documented way adds text to context or description without overwriting concurrent edits, or the replace-only behaviour is stated in the tool description
context:
Imported on 2026-10-28 from the BenchBox tracker item(s): todo-db-update-item-not-before-clear-noop-20261023, todo-db-not-before-clear-and-field-append-20261028. Those items stay open in BenchBox to track the dependency.

In todo-db 0.10.1, store.op_update clears not_before and context when given an empty string (src/todo_db/store.py, op_update), and the changelog documents not_before="" as the way to clear a hold. The reports may therefore come from the MCP client bridge dropping empty strings, or from an older build. Reproduce through todo-db-mcp 0.10.1 on a scratch item before changing code. The append-mode request in the second source item is tracked as update-item-append-mode-and-field-limits.

Source context (todo-db-not-before-clear-and-field-append-20261028): Seen while closing items held until 2026-11-02 after the calendar waits were waived: clearing with an empty string was accepted but the hold stayed. The note-prepend workaround reads then rewrites the whole context field.
description:
The tracker says `not_before=""` clears a hold, and `take` tells callers to use it. Called through the MCP bridge in a coding-agent session on 2026-10-23, `update_item(id, not_before="")` returned `E_STATE operation produced no state change` (and with a context field alongside it changed only the context), so the hold stayed. `not_before=null` was also a no-op. The only way to release the hold was to set a near-future timestamp and wait. Reproduce, then fix in todo-db (argument handling drops empty strings, or the clear path is not wired), add a regression test, and make `take`'s hint accurate.

update_item with not_before set to an empty string does not clear a hold, so an item held to a future date cannot be released early; the only workaround is to set not_before a few seconds ahead, wait, then take. update_item also replaces text fields wholesale, so adding a note to context requires reading the field and writing it back. Both cost extra steps and risk overwriting concurrent edits.
